in_logic_compiler_proof.statement: The refund binary b8ed5ec2...7bb8 was produced by the CakeML compiler inside HOL4 on 2026-11-04. The HOL theorems about it are machine-model theorems with open premises (M1 is open; ROADMAP: M1 and integration EXIT NOT_ESTABLISHED). This work runs no HOL, proves no premise and uses no theorem. The sink treats the binary as a trusted program and believes exactly one output per request.
in_logic_compiler_proof.status: NOT_ESTABLISHED for the running executable; nothing is added here

linked_records.what: Wave Gate 1: this binary and the Slice 1 Dafny refund checker gave equal answers on a finite corpus. It is the only link from the binary to the approved refund spec. A finite test; not run again here; not enforced by the sink.

native_wal_crash_tested.statement: For the recorded requests, kills, damaged files, stand-in binaries and races: a record appeared only after the binary printed the one accept frame of that request, at most once per request id, only on the present state hash and state values, and never below the ratchet; every complete COMMITTED line had its record in the WAL after the recovery. The order lock, record, F_FULLFSYNC, ratchet entry, F_FULLFSYNC, lock released, answer was OBSERVED with an interposer for one traced commit, one traced recovery and one traced init, not for every commit. An answer with code 19 (OUTCOME_UNKNOWN) or 20 (DISPATCH_FAILED) can leave a committed record that was not dispatched. See the keys suite and mutations.
native_wal_crash_tested.status: finite tests passed on one machine
native_wal_crash_tested.what_it_is_not: A SIGKILL keeps the page cache: no test here cuts power or stops the kernel. The system-call order is observed with a dyld interposer inside the sink process; that the drive stores the data is not observed.

note: A record of real tool runs on one machine. It is not Forge gate evidence. A test count is not a proof. No time and no size is in this record.
os_kernel_assumption: macOS Darwin kernel: flock is exclusive and is released when a process ends; a write of 64 bytes with O_APPEND goes to the end of the file; pipes carry the bytes that were written; fcntl(F_FULLFSYNC) returns 0 only after the drive was asked to store the data.
APFS and the physical SSD firmware keep data that F_FULLFSYNC reported as stored, also at power loss. NOT tested.

Mach-O loader and dyld start the refund binary and the sink as their files say; the CakeML basis C code (basis_ffi) and libSystem inside the refund binary do what the HOL model of the foreign functions says. NOT proved, NOT tested here beyond the recorded requests.
rustc 1.92.0, LLVM and the Rust standard library compile and run sink.rs as written. They are unverified and in the trusted base.

The two ledger files, the refund binary file and the environment of the sink are out of reach of an attacker. FNV-1a-128 and CRC-32 authenticate nothing. The sink does not hash the binary: this script does, before and after each run.
A restore of BOTH ledger files (or of the volume) to an older state is not detected on one machine. Recorded as observed in case rollback.
The consumer of the COMMITTED lines treats the request id as an idempotency key. Delivery is at most once per commit; replay prints effects again.

source_proof.statement: src/silicon_sink/sink.rs is NOT proved. The Dafny proofs of Slice 1 (RefundFinality.Check), of the finality protocol model and of the sink core model are not connected to this program. The Ed25519 token of Slice 1 is not used: the sink and the binary are one trust domain.
